summary: Backend tests for Central de IA (Groq + multi-provider credentials, encryption, masking, audit, authz). 15/16 tests pass. Fixed one AttributeError blocking GET/PUT /admin/ai-provider (missing ai.get_api_key). One remaining issue: sandbox does NOT fall back to test-mode when all configured keys fail — it returns provider='unavailable' with a generic error instead of the spec-required '[modo teste]'/provider='test'.

critical.issue: admin.py calls ai.get_api_key() at lines 195 and 341, but lib/ai.py only defines has_any_key(). Every call raised AttributeError → HTTP 500. This broke the very PUT /admin/ai-provider check requested in the review (accept default_provider='groq'). RCA: rename/refactor missed a call-site. FIX APPLIED: added a back-compat alias `async def get_api_key(): return await has_any_key()` in /app/backend/lib/ai.py. All three endpoints now return 200. Recommend the main agent replace the alias with a proper call or keep it explicitly.

When the credential chain is NON-empty but every provider call fails (e.g. only an invalid legacy AI_API_KEY is configured), ai.generate() returns provider='unavailable' with 'Não consegui responder agora por uma instabilidade…' instead of the mock reply. Spec requires falling back to test-mode ('[modo teste]' prefix, provider='test'). Suggested fix in lib/ai.py::generate(): after the fallback loop, when last_error is set, return _mock_reply(...) / 'test' / 'mock' instead of the 'unavailable' string. Reproduce: DB has a legacy platform_settings.AI_API_KEY with an invalid value → POST /api/sandbox/chat → response.provider=='unavailable'.

action_items: Decide on ai.get_api_key alias vs proper rename to has_any_key at admin.py:195 and admin.py:341 (I added an alias to unblock; main agent may prefer explicit).
Fix generate() fallback: when chain is non-empty but all providers fail, degrade to _mock_reply / provider='test' per spec, so /api/sandbox/chat always answers in test mode instead of 'unavailable'.
Consider clearing/rotating the legacy platform_settings.AI_API_KEY (encrypted invalid key present in the demo DB) — it is silently consumed by the fallback chain and causes the unavailable response.
critical_code_review_comments: lib/ai.py: attempt_chain silently accepts a legacy key that later fails 100% of calls, leading to 'unavailable' responses; either surface this in /admin/health or degrade to test mode.
routers/admin.py:285 and :306 use `ai._decrypt_key` (private helper). Consider exposing a public function to avoid the noqa: SLF001 pattern.
PUT /api/admin/ai/credentials stores whatever payload arrives without live-probing (documented as intentional). Consider adding a server-side 'require_valid=true' flag for future hardening.

GET /api/admin/ai/models returns 200 even when the credential is invalid (falls back to curated list from list_provider_models exception handler). Review request allows this ('200 or 400, never 500 or leak key') and no leak occurred, but semantics are worth documenting.
seed_data_creation: Test creates and deletes a single groq credential with the fake key 'gsk_invalid_test_0000000000'. Cleanup via module-scoped fixture teardown. No permanent seed data added.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Cookie auth: /api/auth/login sets `atende_session` with Secure flag; over http httpx won't send it via the cookie jar. The test file manually sets 'Cookie: atende_session=<token>' header — reuse this pattern. Fake groq key used everywhere: 'gsk_invalid_test_0000000000' — grep any response/log for this substring to detect key leaks. All 4 security assertions (no plaintext in PUT response, GET list, audit-logs, backend logs) currently PASS. The one remaining functional gap is the sandbox fallback (see backend_issues).
rca of the issue: 1) ai.get_api_key AttributeError: refactor from single-key model to multi-credential renamed the function to has_any_key but left two call-sites in admin.py. Fix: add alias or rename call-sites. 2) Sandbox 'unavailable': ai.generate returns a hard error string when every candidate in the fallback chain raises; the review contract expects a graceful degradation to _mock_reply when no working credential exists. Current code only degrades when the chain is empty, not when it is exhausted.
